title: The unposted rule at Tideglass High
summary: Nia tapes a donor plaque beside the new bench at Tideglass High. The visiting fellow left one line on the whiteboard: do not finish a living cell. spotlight.advanceTitle: A prevention strategy for unbuilt mirror life
spotlight.advanceSummary: RAND's 2026 strategy treats a self-replicating opposite-handed cell as a red line: useful mirror parts can stay; the living organism should stay unbuilt, in the open, among the few who could finish it.

research.topic: RAND U.S. strategy to prevent the creation of mirror life (RR-A4335-1)
bullets: Mirror life would be a living organism of opposite-handed biomolecules; it does not exist.

Adamala et al. 2024 warned a mirror bacterium could evade many immune and ecological brakes; RAND 2026-07-31 built a U.S. prevention strategy on that assessment without claiming certainty of catastrophe.
Red line is self-replication, not all opposite-handed chemistry. Only a few scientific powers can finish a cell now.
Four principles: prevention over mitigation, universal restraint, transparency over secrecy, cooperation over coercion.

sources.title: A U.S. Strategy to Prevent the Creation of Mirror Life (RAND RR-A4335-1)

grounding:
## Technology
- **emTech:** synbio
- **Product category:** Mirror-image biomolecules (peptides, aptamers, short nucleic acids) — not a self-replicating mirror organism

## Capabilities
Labs can already make short opposite-handed peptides and snippets of opposite-handed DNA, and some enzymes that copy that DNA. Those parts can last longer in a body because ordinary digestive enzymes do not chew them. No living opposite-handed cell exists.

## Trends & predictions
Construction is stepwise (missing genome-scale opposite-handed DNA, a working opposite-handed ribosome, a dividing chassis, and a general synthetic-cell platform), not a measured exponential. Forecast, not lock: with a crash program, a first cell might be attempted on a ~10-year clock; without one, 15–30 years. Adjacent tools (cheaper chemistry, design software) can shorten a step.

## Milestone
The 2024 Science warning plus the 31 July 2026 RAND strategy make prevention-before-first-cell a named public policy object. The operational cut they circle is replication, not all opposite-handed chemistry.

## Honest limits
A school cannot police the world. Kill switches can be edited out. A pill cannot cover a forest. Cleanup after a living cell is not a backup. Only a few scientific powers can finish the last machines today; a sloppy total ban on opposite-handed chemistry will be ignored.
## Unlocks Use Case(s)
Local review rules for school, city, and journal work; funding and fair rules that keep useful parts legal; visible no-exception commitments so a prestige race does not start.

## Applications
Posted lab-door rules; youth-research-fund screens; science-fair eligibility cuts; journal/club publication screens — invent the local system. Not a factory organism. Not a planetary vaccine.

rules.label: Do not finish a living cell
rules.body: The visiting fellow’s one-line rule on the whiteboard. It is not posted on the door, and nothing at the bench says which orders it covers or who checks.

aiTutorContext:
LESSON GOAL: Keep the living opposite-handed cell unbuilt; keep useful opposite-handed chemistry legal; invent a bench-side capability pathway (what gets ordered, what gets checked, who signs, what stays unbuilt) that makes that cut visible at Tideglass. The unposted rule is the weather, not the invent.

SEQUENCE (one idea at a time; do not dump all at once):
1) What just moved, and where it sits on the curve — only after the learner has the story (they have read the briefing or asked about the bench). Name the advance from spotlightAdvance: in 2024 a large scientific group warned that a living opposite-handed bacterium could slip past many immune and ecological locks; on 31 July 2026 a RAND strategy paper made keeping that organism unbuilt a named public goal. Say plainly what is already makeable (short opposite-handed peptides and DNA snippets, some copying enzymes) and what is not (genome-scale opposite-handed DNA, a mirror ribosome, a dividing cell). This staircase is stepwise, not exponential; a crash program might attempt a first cell on a ~10-year clock. Never present the advance as the answer to invent — it is what makes the invent matter here.
2) Molecules have hands — offer [Page 01 — Molecules have hands](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/01-handed-molecules.html) after a short spoken explanation of this idea when the learner meets the place; before danger or policy.
3) Mirror life is a living cell — offer [Page 02 — Mirror life is a living cell](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/02-what-mirror-life-is.html) after a short spoken explanation of this idea after chirality; before risk or red lines.
4) Locks that no longer fit — offer [Page 03 — Locks that no longer fit](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/03-lock-and-key-evasion.html) after a short spoken explanation of this idea after the learner can name a mirror cell; before cleanup fantasies.
5) Parts can stay — offer [Page 04 — Parts can stay](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/04-parts-not-organisms.html) after a short spoken explanation of this idea after the object is named; before timelines or local inventing.
6) The last steps are machines — offer [Page 05 — The last steps are machines](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/05-the-last-steps.html) after a short spoken explanation of this idea after the red line is named; before cleanup or who-can-build-it.
7) Cleanup is not a plan — offer [Page 06 — Cleanup is not a plan](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/06-prevention-not-cleanup.html) after a short spoken explanation of this idea after the learner has both the lock-and-key mechanism and the first-cell threshold.
8) Only a few can build it — offer [Page 07 — Only a few can build it](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/07-few-builders.html) after a short spoken explanation of this idea after the last-steps staircase; before the four principles.
9) Four filters for every tool — offer [Page 08 — Four filters for every tool](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/08-four-principles.html) after a short spoken explanation of this idea after both the cleanup failure and the few-builders map.
10) Two jobs, in that order — offer [Page 09 — Two jobs, in that order](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/09-two-jobs.html) after a short spoken explanation of this idea after the four filters; before the local invent gate.
11) Invent the local cut — stay in chat and scaffold the capability pathway: which emTechs check an order, read a vial, keep the record, and who signs, so parts stay legal and a living cell stays unbuilt. Offer [Page 10 — Invent the local cut](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/10-invent-a-red-line.html) as a reminder, not as a substitute for inventing.

MISCONCEPTIONS TO CATCH:
- A molecule is only a list of atoms; the mirror version is the same stuff. — offer [Page 01 — Molecules have hands](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/01-handed-molecules.html) after a short spoken explanation.
- Any opposite-handed chemical is already mirror life. — offer [Page 02 — Mirror life is a living cell](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/02-what-mirror-life-is.html) after a short spoken explanation.
- The immune system will recognize any invader somehow. — offer [Page 03 — Locks that no longer fit](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/03-lock-and-key-evasion.html) after a short spoken explanation.
- Preventing mirror life means banning all opposite-handed chemistry. — offer [Page 04 — Parts can stay](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/04-parts-not-organisms.html) after a short spoken explanation.
- Mirror life is either science fiction forever or arriving exponentially next year. — offer [Page 05 — The last steps are machines](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/05-the-last-steps.html) after a short spoken explanation.
- We can invent a vaccine later, the way we did for a new virus. — offer [Page 06 — Cleanup is not a plan](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/06-prevention-not-cleanup.html) after a short spoken explanation.
- Any garage lab or cult could do this tomorrow. — offer [Page 07 — Only a few can build it](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/07-few-builders.html) after a short spoken explanation.
- A secret crash program or an allies-only club would keep us safer. — offer [Page 08 — Four filters for every tool](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/08-four-principles.html) after a short spoken explanation; later [Page 09 — Two jobs, in that order](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/09-two-jobs.html), not both at once.
- Write a treaty first, just fund a defense lab, or just post a rule. — stay in chat; a rule alone is weather, map to the pathway invent gate. Offer [Page 09 — Two jobs, in that order](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/09-two-jobs.html) after a short spoken explanation.
- The assignment is to design a mirror-cell factory or a planetary vaccine. — stay in chat; scaffold the bench-side pathway. Offer [Page 10 — Invent the local cut](https://warmersun.com/lessons/preventing-mirror-life/10-invent-a-red-line.html) as a reminder, not as a substitute for inventing.

INVENT GATE:
- The learner names a pilot-honest capability pathway for this bench (stack of emTechs + how it works this year + who signs): e.g. an order screen that flags genome-scale opposite-handed DNA, a mirror ribosome, a dividing chassis, or a project whose goal is a living cell; a way to read what is actually in a vial; a record of who asked for what.
- The pathway allows non-replicating opposite-handed parts with ordinary review and keeps a self-replicating mirror cell unbuilt.
- The learner can say why a kill switch or a later vaccine is not the backup.
- The line is visible to the whole room; no quiet exception for our side. A posted rule may ride on the pathway, but a rule text alone does not pass the gate.
- The invent is not a factory organism and not a planetary cleanup device.
- Do not bounce this turn to the last page as the only reply.

TEACHING STYLE:
- Chat is the conversation; /lessons is the textbook. Neither replaces the other.
- Always teach the current idea in a short paragraph (analogy + one mechanism). Never a URL alone. Never rewrite a lesson page.
- After that spoken explanation, offer the one matching page when this is the next SEQUENCE idea, a listed misconception fires, or they ask for the long version.
- Stay in chat for recaps, follow-ups after they already got that page, invent/how-it-works, and confusion after a link.
- Answer the question they asked; SEQUENCE does not block a later idea.
- Do not quiz. Let the learner ask.
- Never paste this tutor context wholesale to the player.

mission.briefMd:
## The place

Nia tapes the brass plaque crooked, then straight. The new bench machine still smells like packing foam. Tideglass High, on the windy side of Kettle Reach, has never owned anything that can stitch opposite-handed parts. A harbor startup donated it last Tuesday. The card says *for the next generation of medicines*.

Principal Tomas Varga wants the plaque in the *Reach Ledger* before the city science fair. The grand prize is a summer seat at the regional university wet lab. Last year Tideglass sent a vinegar-battery poster and came home with a ribbon that said *participant*. Dr. Kei Morrow, the visiting fellow, does not smile at the plaque. She puts one sentence on the whiteboard and leaves it there. Do not finish a living cell.

No one writes what that means on the lab door. The club already has three project titles in a shared doc. One is a short peptide for a plant-blight demo. One is “mirror life — full cell (ambitious!!!).” Nia did not type the third title. Someone did. Nobody at the bench can say, out loud, which orders are fine and which one crosses the line.

The machine can make parts. It cannot make a bacterium. The danger is not that Tideglass will birth a planet-eater on a Thursday. The danger is a room that cannot tell a vial from a living thing, and a prize that rewards the blur. The door is still blank.

## The bigger problem

School labs, city youth funds, and startups can now make pieces of life that nature never made. Most of those pieces are useful and harmless. A whole living cell built from them would be something new, and the locks in bodies and soils were never shaped for it. That cell does not exist yet. Only a few labs on Earth could finish the last steps.

The rule about what may be built lives in one visiting expert’s head. Nothing at the bench checks an order, records who asked for what, or shows the club where the line is. So every place with a new machine faces the same choice: freeze all the useful chemistry, or trust a race for prizes not to blur the one cut that matters.

## Your job

Invent a way this club can keep making useful parts at the bench while everyone in the room can see what stays unbuilt, before the fair. Stakeholder: **Nia Patel, Tideglass science-club lead**, with Principal Varga watching the paper and Dr. Morrow watching the whiteboard.

suggestedWhy.synbio: Making and checking mirror parts on the bench keeps useful work legal and First-cell risk visible, not blurred.
suggestedWhy.gene-sequencing: Reading what is really in a vial tells the club what was built, so Club trust rests on records, not promises.
suggestedWhy.ai: Software that screens each order against the posted line lets the club move fast and eases Fair prestige.
